::: {.entry-meta}
[decision]{.chip .decision} [new component]{.chip .built} Entry 63 · milestone JOREK (alongside M4)
:::

JOREK is a nonlinear extended magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) code for edge-localised modes
(ELMs), disruptions and tearing modes in realistic X-point geometry. The toolkit's
transport loop has no MHD stability model: its pedestal is prescribed or predicted by
EPEDNN, and the sawtooth model is a reduced trigger. JOREK has been open source since
this year, so it can be used as an independent open (Tier A) reference for those parts.

The owner chose the scope ([OQ-37](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-37)). JOREK is an external reference code. It runs
outside the JAX loop, never inside compiled code, and is never a runtime dependency of
a surrogate. The first use is linear pedestal-stability scans over toroidal mode
number on the ITER hybrid case, then an internal-kink check for the sawtooth model,
then MAST-U. Nonlinear ELM runs are later reference runs only. Disruption studies are
outside the brief.

We built JOREK from source on a CPU cluster with our own build of the MUMPS sparse
solver, because the cluster's shared JOREK libraries were not available to us. Two
input changes were needed for the GNU Fortran compiler and the solver choice. Neither
changes a value. As a check that does not depend on our code, we ran JOREK's own
regression cases against the reference data the JOREK team publishes
([3 of 4 upstream regression cases reproduce their public reference data: MAST-U grid and equilibrium (largest difference 2.0e-5, tolerance 1e-4), MAST equilibrium with coils (1.2e-10), and one implicit tearing-mode step (4.1e-13, tolerance 1e-12); the full-MHD kink case was not run because its upstream input is out of date for this code version]{.claim}[C-210](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-210){.cid .st-measured}). One case could not be run: its input predates a consistency check
in the current code, and fixing it would mean changing physics inputs.

A single one-hour CPU job then repeated the regression cases on the compute nodes and
measured the cost of an implicit time step on the MAST-U X-point grid
([all three regression cases pass on a 256-core AMD node; one implicit step on the MAST-U X-point grid (8050 elements, toroidal modes n = 0 and 1) takes 5.8 s at 2 ranks x 16 threads, 6.7 s at 4 x 32 and 8.1 s at 2 x 64; the whole job used 22.4 core-hours]{.claim}[C-211](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-211){.cid .st-measured}). That cost sets the size of the compute request for the
stability scans.

Where this stands: build and regression checks done; physics settings for the first
stability runs await the owner ([OQ-39](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-39)).

Technical details → [JOREK](../technical/jorek.qmd#build). Decision → [OQ-37](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-37).
